Sam —

Appreciate the context. Short answers up front: yes on a two-week extension; and both packaging options are viable but favor different teams. Below is a concise comparison and a proposed playbook.

Summary comparison (high level):
- Flexible credit pool: single prepaid credit bucket you draw from. Pros: predictable unit economics, easy to top up, no per-hour metering to manage. Cons: you pay for unused tokens if forecast is off; less visibility into minute-level concurrency.
- Hourly block add-on: reserve N GPU-hours for burst windows. Pros: predictable burst capacity and latency SLOs during heavy tests; easy for eng to reason about concurrency. Cons: more expensive per-token if utilization is low; requires us to provision capacity in a particular window.

Proposed pilot playbook: 1) Extend pilot 14 days (no additional fee). 2) Convert existing trial credits into a small flexible pool sized to your estimate + a one-time hourly block (24 GPU-hours) for scheduled ingest runs. 3) If hourly block unused, we roll a partial credit back into the flexible pool at 50% conversion (to avoid reserve cost).

I’m looping Laura (pricing) to confirm numbers and Marcus (solutions) to scope the 24-hour burst. We can provide a one-page amendment and a short SOW.

—Karthik
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
